166.summary: Fifth volume of Atila Sinke Guimarães's eleven-volume Collection on Vatican II, Eli, Eli, Lamma Sabacthani?, published by Tradition in Action and continuing the argument of Animus Delendi I. Working largely through quotations from progressivist theologians and prelates, the Brazilian traditionalist author documents what he regards as a deliberate 'desire to destroy' the Church's traditional structures and the Catholic social order that grew up around them. Dense, heavily footnoted and frankly polemical, it is written for readers already familiar with the post-conciliar debates.

240.summary: Marian Therese Horvat gathers the history, favors and miracles attributed to Our Lady of Good Success — the title under which the Blessed Virgin appeared to Mother Mariana de Jesús Torres in the Conceptionist convent of Quito, Ecuador, between the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries. A companion to her Our Lady of Good Success: Prophecies for Our Times, it recounts the story of the miraculous statue still venerated in Quito and testimonies of graces received by those who have invoked her. Published by Tradition in Action.

316.summary: Edición de bolsillo en español del Diario de santa Faustina Kowalska (1905-1938), la religiosa polaca a quien Jesús confió el mensaje de la Divina Misericordia. En sus cuadernos, escritos por obediencia a su confesor entre 1934 y 1938, Faustina recoge sus conversaciones interiores con Cristo, la petición de la imagen «Jesús, en Ti confío», la Coronilla y la Fiesta de la Misericordia, junto con la crónica de su vida cotidiana en el convento y de sus sufrimientos. Publicado por los Padres Marianos (Marian Press), custodios oficiales del mensaje.

91.summary: Lecciones de la Virgen María para aprender a vivir en la Divina Voluntad y conocer los males de vivir de voluntad humana. El libro pertenece a los escritos atribuidos a Luisa Piccarreta (1865-1947), la mística italiana de Corato, en los que María enseña, mes a mes, el camino de abandono en la Voluntad de Dios; se lee como devocionario, una lección por día, y su difusión responde a la causa de beatificación de Luisa, todavía en curso.

31.summary: Comentario al Apocalipsis del jesuita argentino Leonardo Castellani (1899-1981), escritor, filósofo y uno de los pensadores católicos más originales del siglo XX en lengua española. Fruto de muchos años de estudio del último libro de la Escritura, lo expone con fidelidad a la Tradición y una claridad poco común, en un estilo vibrante y a veces irónico pero siempre sacerdotal, insistiendo en que el Apocalipsis no es un libro de terror sino de esperanza. Ha sido reeditado en España con prólogo de Juan Manuel de Prada.

425.summary: Shawn Carney, president of 40 Days for Life, offers a forty-day companion of short daily readings for anyone taking part in the campaign's prayer vigils — or simply wanting to pray and think more deeply about the culture of life. Each day pairs a brief reflection with Scripture and a prayer, moving from the dignity of every human life to family, forgiveness and hope. Brief enough for a busy morning and meant to be read one day at a time.

152.summary: Una colección ilustrada de cuentos para niños en torno a tres virtudes —el valor, el amor y la honestidad—, pensada para leer en voz alta y comentar en familia. Cada relato presenta a personajes que se enfrentan a una pequeña dificultad y descubren, sin sermones, por qué merece la pena ser valiente, cariñoso y sincero. Un libro sencillo para las primeras lecturas y para la educación en valores de los más pequeños.

267.summary: "Every scribe instructed in the Kingdom of Heaven is like a householder who brings forth out of his storeroom things both new and old. " Matthew 13:52 St. Thérèse of Lisieux, well acquainted with the Kingdom and famous for showering roses from Heaven, has done it again. In this little book, apt quotations from the Little Flower appear alongside beautiful old fashioned block print images of the traditional Stations of the Cross. The combination provides all little souls - from children, converts, and beginners in the spiritual life to those who have accompanied Jesus for decades - with a fresh set of meditations on Jesus' infinite love as expressed in His Passion and Death. Each Station begins with the customary "We adore Thee, O Christ, and we bless Thee . . ." and ends with an Our Father, Hail Mary, or Glory Be. Following the fourteen Stations are St. Thérèse's Prayer to the Holy Face, her sister Celine's painting of the Holy Face (after the Shroud of Turin), the indulgenced Prayer Before a Crucifix, and a brief explanation of indulgences. St. Thérèse described prayer as "a lifting up of the heart; a simple glance heavenwards; a cry of gratitude and of love, in the midst of trials as well as amidst joys. It is something great, something supernatural, which expands the soul and unites it with Jesus. "With this book, she invites readers to join her in a simple glance heavenwards, a cry of gratitude and love, something supernatural to unite the soul with Jesus as He proceeds step by step, Station by Station, to His Passion and Death for love of us. Walk the Way of the Cross with this Doctor of the Church as she brings forth from her Mother's storeroom a blend of prayers both old and new. Perfect for individual devotion, group prayer, and congregational use in a parish, St. Thérèse's little way of spiritual childhood and the Stations of the Cross blend to produce a fragrant offering of love.
